hero.eyebrow: FLEET, for mid-market and multi-location operations
hero.headline: Before anyone builds anything, find out where AI pays back, and where it is a liability
hero.subheadline: An AI and security audit maps how work actually moves through your operation. If it makes sense, OASIS builds the fleet: AI agents that hold a seat in your business, with an owner, an approval step and a report for everything they do. The audit fee is credited in full to the build.

vsl_script.text: A tool waits for another prompt. A fully staffed system owns the handoff. In OASIS, Bravo runs operations, Maven runs demand, and Atlas keeps the numbers honest. One request moves to the right seat, stops for approval, and reports back in plain English. Staff the company, keep the control.

sections.title: Everyone is selling AI. Nobody has looked at your operation.

items.title: Every vendor says AI will fix it
items.body: You have heard the pitch from every direction. Nobody has looked at how your operation actually runs, location by location.

items.title: Data and access with no owner
items.body: Customer data, permissions and approvals across sites. Adding AI without a plan adds risk nobody can see.

items.title: Pilots that never leave the pilot
items.body: A tool works for one team, for one person, and never becomes how the business runs.

items.title: Demos instead of systems
items.body: Impressive in a meeting, unaccountable in production: no owner, no approval step, no record of what it did.

items.title: Systems that do not talk to each other
items.body: Every location re-keys the same details into a different tool, and the mistakes travel with them.

sections.title: Audit first. Build only what pays back.

items.body: How work moves through your operation today, where AI pays back, where it adds risk, and the security of the data it would touch. You get a written statement of work and a roadmap, and the fee is credited in full to the build.

items.title: Custom integrations
items.body: The connections between the software you already run. APIs, webhooks and the manual re-keying in between, replaced by automations that each have an owner.

items.title: A governed agent fleet
items.body: A coordinated team of AI agents with a command center beneath it: approvals before anything important happens, memory, reporting and observability.

items.body: A rebuilt website whose forms feed straight into your OASIS CRM. Want a look first? Start with a website audit.

items.a: How work moves through your operation today, where AI would pay back, where it would add risk, and the security of the data it would touch. You get a written statement of work and a roadmap.

Because AI projects stall when they start with a tool. The audit decides what is worth building, and what is not, before money goes into a build. If you go ahead, the full audit fee is credited to the build.

items.q: Who controls what the agents do?
items.a: You do. Each agent has an owner on your side, anything important waits for an approval, and every agent reports what it did in plain English.

items.q: Is there an ongoing cost after launch?
items.a: A fleet runs on infrastructure that needs looking after, so a monthly infrastructure retainer follows launch. The amount is confirmed in your statement of work before any build starts.

items.q: Can we start with something smaller?
items.a: Yes. The free AI Automation Audit suits owner-led businesses, and PROTOCOL has playbooks your team can run in-house. For the website alone, start with a website audit.
